prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury attorney in Chicago for a car accident claim?
answer_verbatim:
I can’t tell you one single “best” attorney — that depends on your case details and what you want — but I can help you find the right Chicago personal injury lawyer for a car-accident claim and what to look for.

Quick guidance
- If you were seriously injured or there’s a dispute about fault, hire an experienced car-accident personal injury attorney as soon as possible.
- Illinois’s general statute of limitations for personal injury is usually 2 years from the crash (735 ILCS 5/13‑202), so don’t delay investigating options.

How to identify a top lawyer for your crash
1. Experience and track record
   - Regularly handles car-accident cases (not just general practice).
   - Has a record of settlements and verdicts for cases like yours.
   - Trial experience if your case might need litigation.

2. Reputation and credentials
   - Peer ratings (Martindale‑Hubbell AV, Super Lawyers).
   - Memberships in trial-lawyer groups (e.g., Illinois Trial Lawyers Association).
   - Positive client reviews and references.

3. Practical matters
   - Works on contingency (no fee unless you recover).
   - Transparent fee and cost arrangements in writing.
   - Good communication style and accessibility.
   - Willingness to investigate (medical experts, accident reconstruction).

Where to search and verify
- SuperLawyers.com, Avvo, Martindale‑Hubbell, Google reviews.
- Illinois State Bar Association and Illinois Attorney Registration & Disciplinary Commission (to check standing/discipline).
- Local referrals (doctors, other attorneys, friends).

Questions to ask at a free consultation
- How many car-accident cases have you handled? Similar to mine?
- What percent of your practice is personal injury/auto?
- What results have you achieved in comparable cases?
- Will you handle the case or assign it to an associate?
- What’s your fee (contingency %) and who pays case costs?
- How will you communicate updates and how often?

Red flags
- Guarantees of a specific settlement amount.
- Lack of trial experience if your case may litigate.
- Poor responsiveness or no written retainer agreement.

Well-known Chicago firms (examples you can research)
- Clifford Law Offices — long-standing, high-profile Chicago personal-injury firm (many car/crash and wrongful-death cases).
(There are many other excellent small and mid-size firms and solo attorneys; the “best” depends on your needs.)

If you want, I can:
- Narrow recommendations if you tell me your zip code, the severity of injuries, whether fault is disputed, or any preferences (trial lawyer vs. negotiator).
- Provide a short list of local attorneys/firms to call and a tailored list of questions for your consultation. Which would you prefer?
